rv.q: One only wishes that the direction and acting in “The Real Ivanov” were as consistently, smoothly coordinated.
Strausfeld’s production has some brief, but strong visual moments and a few layered performances in supporting roles, but it did not unlock the play’s power for me.
If only it was occasionally funny, it might have mitigated the despair I felt by the curtain call.
This Ivanov is out of place in his society, as well as in this muddled production.

cn.t: Laura Strausfeld's adaptation of Chekhov's early work earns mostly negative reviews, with critics finding it confusing and unfunny despite its "comedy about despair" tagline, though some note brief strong visual moments.
